The Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute later recommended everyone to watch the full unedited address on the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library YouTube account
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: The dispute began with an Ontario government advertisement that used excerpts from Ronald Reagan’s 1987 radio address criticizing tariffs. The speech was real, though the ad edited and rearranged portions of it and did not include the full context of Reagan’s comments about tariffs on Japan. On October 23, 2025, President Donald Trump called the ad fake, said it interfered with Supreme Court cases over his tariffs, and announced that he was ending trade negotiations with Canada. A day later, he said he guessed it was made using AI, an allegation for which the contemporaneous reporting cited here offered no supporting production evidence. Ontario Premier Doug Ford said the province would pause the ad after its initial World Series broadcasts. On October 25, Trump announced an additional 10% tariff on Canadian goods. Reporting did not make clear which products would be covered or how the increase would interact with existing exemptions for qualifying goods under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Ag
